topics.topic: Ol Chiki Script – 100 Years of Linguistic Empowerment
topics.why_in_news: Centenary celebrations of Ol Chiki script highlighted its role in preservation, empowerment and cultural identity of the Santali language and tribal communities.
prelims_quick_notes: Ol Chiki is script used for Santali language.
Santali belongs to Austroasiatic language family.
Script played major role in tribal linguistic empowerment.
Santali included in Eighth Schedule of Constitution.
Language preservation linked with cultural identity protection.
Tribal languages important component of India’s diversity.
Script standardised Santali literary and educational development.
important_facts: Pandit Raghunath Murmu known as Guru Gomke.
Santali added to Eighth Schedule through 92nd Constitutional Amendment.
Santali spoken mainly in Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal and neighbouring regions.
Austroasiatic family also includes Mundari and Ho-related linguistic groups.
key_highlights: Centenary celebrated as milestone in linguistic empowerment.
Focus on preservation of indigenous knowledge systems.
Recognition of tribal identity and cultural heritage emphasised.
Promotion of multilingual and inclusive cultural policies discussed.
exam_relevance: Important for History, Culture and Tribal Studies.
Useful for linguistic diversity and constitutional language topics.
Can be linked with tribal identity and cultural preservation.
prelims_traps: Ol Chiki associated with Santali language.
Santali belongs to Austroasiatic family, not Dravidian family.
92nd Constitutional Amendment added Santali to Eighth Schedule.
